title: Which businesses are using AI technology?
gist: The St. Louis Fed uses Ramp AI Index data (now in FRED) to show more than half of US businesses paid for AI by September 2026, with industry mattering more than size and Anthropic now the most widely paid-for provider.

insights.claim: According to the Ramp AI Index, as of September 2026 more than half of all businesses paid for an AI product or service, with adoption jumping after ChatGPT's late-2022 launch and rising steadily since.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Enterprise AI adoption has crossed the majority mark.

insights.claim: Adoption has risen for businesses of every size and is spreading fastest at large and medium-sized firms, while small businesses lag.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Next adoption wave depends on small-firm uptake.

insights.claim: Industry matters much more than size: information leads, finance and insurance are close behind, then manufacturing, retail, health care, construction, and accommodation and food services.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Software and finance are the leading AI-spend sectors.

insights.claim: OpenAI surged in early 2023 and rose through most of 2025 but has leveled off since, while Anthropic gained steadily from 2024, accelerated sharply in early 2026, and is now the most widely paid-for provider tracked.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Business-paid AI share has shifted toward Anthropic and away from OpenAI.

insights.claim: xAI remains a much smaller third provider in the Ramp data.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog

insights.claim: The Ramp series do not capture free AI tools, AI features built into other software, or usage intensity such as token spend, so they understate total AI use.
insights.speaker: St. Louis Fed — FRED Blog
insights.so_what: Treat adoption as a floor and a measure of paid breadth, not depth.
